correctness.rationale: For N=n−1, A=c00 and B=c11 determine the total mixed count and δ=last−first determines the mixed-count imbalance. Thus Parseval must be applied within δ buckets, with the two same-endpoint contributions added before squaring. The transfer matrix has entries weighted by 1/2 and an additional 1/2 for the initial bit, as used in RESULT.md lines 23–35. Equality in the row triangle inequalities at a unit-modulus eigenvalue enforces λ²=1 and both diagonal phases equal to λ. Compactness and a uniform resolvent bound give exponential decay off the two torus neighborhoods, including potentially defective matrices. At the simple eigenvalue 1, lag-zero and lag-one indicator covariances give Σ=[[5,−3],[−3,5]]/16, det Σ=1/16. The endpoint-sector squared amplitudes sum to 3/8. Conjugation by diag(1,−1) and a global minus sign give the same squared weights at the other peak (one peak on the torus, not four corner peaks). The analytic expansion yields a uniform Gaussian bound and each peak integral is 4π/N before the Fourier normalization. The resulting factor is 3/(4πN), giving the claimed limit and entropy. Inspected RESULT.md, VERIFICATION.md and verify.py without executing the uploaded program. Review-side direct counting, dynamic counts and the run sum independently agree through n=16; the count there is 70,873,180. The two sum methods also agree at n=60,100,160 with nP_n≈0.2446063, 0.2421977, 0.2408783. These are finite checks only.
